title: Structural Load Path Visualization Tool
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a structural load path visualization tool for architectural analysis. Load the GLTFLoader from CDN as well.

SCENE SETUP:
- Dark background (0x1a1a2e) with a grid helper (size 40, divisions 40, color 0x333355).
- Perspective camera at position (12, 10, 12) looking at origin.
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) at (10, 15, 10) casting shadows.
- Load 'CesiumMilkTruck.glb' using GLTFLoader. Scale it to 2x and position it at (0, 0, 0). This model represents a structural reference object on the ground plane. Store a reference in window.__3D_STATE__.truckModel.

STRUCTURAL FRAME SYSTEM:
- Build a 3D structural frame (portal frame) consisting of:
  - 4 vertical columns (BoxGeometry 0.3x4x0.3) at corners: (-4,2,-3), (4,2,-3), (-4,2,3), (4,2,3). Color 0x4488cc.
  - 4 horizontal beams connecting column tops (BoxGeometry spanning between columns, 0.3x0.3xLength). Color 0x44cc88.
  - 2 diagonal braces on the front face (from bottom-left to top-right and bottom-right to top-left of the front face z=-3). Color 0xcc8844.
- Each structural member must be stored in an array window.__3D_STATE__.members[] with properties: {mesh, type:'column'|'beam'|'brace', stress:0, maxStress:100, loadContribution:0}.
- Total member count should be 10 (4 columns + 4 beams + 2 braces).

LOAD APPLICATION SYSTEM:
- Maintain an array of applied loads: window.__3D_STATE__.loads = []
- Users can add point loads by clicking on beams. When a beam is clicked (raycasting), add a downward load arrow (red ArrowHelper, direction (0,-1,0), length proportional to load magnitude) at the click point on the beam.
- Each load has: {id, position:{x,y,z}, magnitude:10, arrowHelper}. Default magnitude is 10 kN.
- Maximum 5 loads can be applied. Track count in window.__3D_STATE__.loadCount.
- Total applied load: window.__3D_STATE__.totalLoad (sum of all magnitudes).

LOAD PATH VISUALIZATION:
- When loads are applied, compute a simplified load path: each load distributes stress to the nearest columns proportionally (inverse distance weighting).
- Stress in each column = sum of (load.magnitude * (1/distance_to_column)) / sum_of_inverse_distances for each load.
- Beams that carry loads get stress equal to the sum of loads directly on them.
- Braces get 30% of the average column stress.
- Visualize stress by changing member color: interpolate from blue (0x4488cc, stress=0) to red (0xff2222, stress>=80).
- Store computed total system stress: window.__3D_STATE__.totalSystemStress (sum of all member stresses).

INTERACTION MODES:
- window.__3D_STATE__.mode can be 'select', 'load', or 'analyze'.
- 'select' mode: clicking a member highlights it yellow and shows its info in the HUD. Store selected member index in window.__3D_STATE__.selectedMember (null or index).
- 'load' mode: clicking a beam adds a load at that point.
- 'analyze' mode: triggers full stress recalculation and color update on all members.
- Switch modes via buttons in the DOM.

KEYBOARD CONTROLS:
- Press '1' to switch to 'select' mode.
- Press '2' to switch to 'load' mode.
- Press '3' to switch to 'analyze' mode.
- Press 'R' to reset all loads (clear loads array, reset all stresses to 0, reset colors to defaults). After reset, loadCount=0, totalLoad=0, totalSystemStress=0.
- Press '+' or '=' to increase the magnitude of the next load to be placed by 5 (window.__3D_STATE__.nextLoadMagnitude, starts at 10, max 50).
- Press '-' to decrease it by 5 (min 5).

HUD / DOM ELEMENTS:
- A top-left panel (id='info-panel') showing: current mode, load count, total load, total system stress, next load magnitude.
- Three buttons: id='btn-select', id='btn-load', id='btn-analyze'.
- A button id='btn-reset' to reset all loads.
- A button id='btn-toggle-paths' that toggles visibility of load path lines (dashed lines from load points down to column bases). Store toggle state in window.__3D_STATE__.pathsVisible (default true).

LOAD PATH LINES:
- When loads exist and paths are visible, draw dashed lines (THREE.LineDashedMaterial, color 0xffaa00) from each load position to the base of each column it distributes to. Store these in window.__3D_STATE__.pathLines[].

STATE OBJECT (window.__3D_STATE__):
- truckModel: reference to loaded GLTF scene
- members: array of {mesh, type, stress, maxStress, loadContribution}
- loads: array of {id, position, magnitude, arrowHelper}
- loadCount: number
- totalLoad: number
- totalSystemStress: number
- mode: 'select'|'load'|'analyze'
- selectedMember: null|number
- nextLoadMagnitude: number (default 10)
- pathsVisible: boolean (default true)
- pathLines: array
- initialized: true (set after everything is ready)
- memberCount: 10
- columnsCount: 4
- beamsCount: 4
- bracesCount: 2
physics_constraints: Load distribution must follow inverse-distance weighting to columns. Total load path contribution must equal total applied load (conservation). Stress values must be non-negative and NaN-free. Member stresses must update consistently when loads are added or removed. Braces receive 30% of average column stress. All stress values reset to 0 on reset.
